header.title: Mahabharat Episode 5: Shantanu Meets Ganga
header.description: The story of Emperor Bharata's wisdom in choosing a successor based on merit, the celestial curse of Mahabhishek and Ganga, and their fateful meeting on the riverbank.

intro.title: The Wisdom of Emperor Bharata
leads: Although Emperor Bharata had many sons, he recognized that none of them possessed the necessary qualities to be good rulers for his citizens.
In a revolutionary act of wisdom, he established that biological connection alone was not enough to claim a throne.
Bharata was celebrated across the land for his balance of mind, impartiality, and sense of inclusion—which is why the nation carries his name.

storyElements.html: Instead of passing the throne to his biological sons, Bharata chose a boy named Vithatha as his successor.
Vithatha was born to Mamata, the wife of Brihaspati's brother, after Brihaspati had forced himself upon her in a moment of indiscretion.
Vithatha grew into a great king who ruled his entire lifetime with exceptional wisdom and balance.
Fourteen generations down from Vithatha came Shantanu, who would become the great-grandfather of the Pandavas and Kauravas.

storyElements.text: The Curse of Mahabhishek and Ganga

storyElements.html: In his previous life, King Shantanu was a noble ruler named Mahabhishek. After living a full life, he entered Devaloka.
One day while Mahabhishek was sitting in Indra's court, goddess Ganga came visiting.
In a moment of unawareness, Ganga's dress fell and her upper body was exposed.
Following proper decorum, everyone in court averted their gaze—except Mahabhishek, who was new to Devaloka and kept staring at her.

bubble.text: You are unfit to stay in Devaloka! Go back and be born as a human being again!

storyElements.html: Indra then noticed that Ganga seemed to be enjoying the attention rather than covering herself.

bubble.text: This is completely inappropriate! You too must go back and be born as a human being. Go through all the pains and pleasures of human existence until you are free from this pride!

storyElements.html: Reborn on Earth as King Shantanu, he had no memory of his past life in Devaloka.
Ganga, however, retained her memories and sought to draw Shantanu toward her.
Shantanu was a fine hunter who would become so engrossed in hunting that it felt like worship to him.
One day, after hunting near the river for weeks on end, intense thirst overtook him when no servants were around. He walked down to the water's edge.
At that moment, Ganga arose from the river as a woman. The instant Shantanu set eyes upon her, he fell completely in love and pleaded with her to marry him.

bubble.text: I will marry you, but on one condition: no matter what I do, you must never ask me why I am doing it!

storyElements.html: In ancient history, women frequently set strict conditions before marriage. For example, when Puru fell in love with the apsara Urvashi, she demanded two conditions: her pet goats had to be protected by his army, and no one could ever see him naked.
When the devas stole her goats in the dark, Puru rushed out, but Indra sent lightning that exposed Puru naked—causing Urvashi to leave him forever.
Over time, as society shifted from matriarchal to patriarchal, women gradually lost this ability to set such conditions.
Madly in love, Shantanu agreed to whatever Ganga asked.
Ganga became his beautiful and wonderful queen, and in time, she became pregnant...
Bound by his promise never to question her actions, King Shantanu awaits the arrival of their firstborn child...
